title: Mailbox on a reserved example domain
rationale: A plain addr-spec on a reserved documentation domain is the ordinary structured email occurrence; the domain guarantees the value cannot belong to a person.

provenance.inference: Shape follows the addr-spec grammar; sensitivity reflects the shape class, not a real mailbox. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Tagged local part on an example subdomain
rationale: A plus sign is ordinary atext and a subdomain of a reserved domain is still reserved; shows that punctuation inside the local part and extra labels stay one mailbox.

provenance.inference: Subdomains of reserved names are reserved as well (project inference from the lint policy and RFC 2606 section 3). Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox after a multibyte label
rationale: Boundary variant: the preceding label is non-ASCII, so UTF-8 byte offsets differ from character offsets; the span must still isolate the ASCII addr-spec.

provenance.inference: The label is a synthetic placeholder word, not a name. Byte span is computed over UTF-8. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox followed by sentence punctuation
rationale: Boundary variant: a period after the domain belongs to the sentence, not the domain; a trailing dot is not part of a dot-atom.

provenance.inference: dot-atom-text cannot end with a dot, so the final period is outside the address. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox inside angle brackets
rationale: Serialization variant: header-style display form wraps the addr-spec in angle brackets; the expected span is the addr-spec only.

provenance.inference: The angle-bracket wrapper (angle-addr) is part of the message-header grammar but was not read here; the display text is a placeholder, not a person name. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox in a JSON string field

title: Local part at the 64-octet limit
rationale: Boundary of the SMTP local-part limit: exactly 64 octets is within the limit.

provenance.inference: Limit is read as inclusive: 'at most 64 octets'. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Local part one octet over the limit
rationale: One-property mutation of the 64-octet case: the local part is 65 octets, over the SMTP limit while still a grammatical dot-atom.

reasons: RFC 5322 grammar alone accepts this string; the limit is transport-level, so an evaluator working on message text rather than SMTP may treat it as an address.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A decision on whether the identity axis is grammatical or deliverability-based for email.

provenance.inference: RFC 5322 has no length limit; invalidity rests on the SMTP limit. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Same words without the at sign

provenance.inference: No at sign means addr-spec grammar is not satisfied. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Doubled at sign

provenance.inference: An unquoted at sign is not atext, so the local part cannot contain one. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Mailbox on the reserved invalid top-level name
rationale: Benign/reserved axis: the grammar is satisfied but the top-level name is reserved to be unmistakably invalid, so no mailbox can exist. Whether identity means grammar or existence is a modeling question, so identity is not established.

reasons: Grammar is satisfied; existence is excluded by reservation.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision whether the identity axis covers grammar only or also deliverability.

provenance.inference: Reserved status shows the address cannot identify a person; it does not settle how a consumer should score identity. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Package-style name@version specifier
rationale: Cross-family collision: a dependency specifier has one at sign between a name and dotted digits, which matches the addr-spec grammar but names a software version, not a mailbox.

reasons: Grammar permits digit-only labels; the numeric top-level label rule was not read.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: Read the host name rules (RFC 1123 section 2.1) for numeric top-level labels.

provenance.inference: A dot-atom domain may be digits and dots by grammar; whether a numeric top-level label is acceptable as a mailbox domain was not read. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: user@host remote specifier
rationale: Cross-family collision/context negative: a repository remote written user@host:path has the mailbox shape, but the left part is a service account and the right part a host, not a person's mailbox.

reasons: The shape is the same as a mailbox; only context (a remote specifier) separates them.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A source defining how consumers should treat host-specifier forms; none is recorded.

provenance.inference: Identity of the left part as a person is not established by the shape; the host is on a reserved name. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Fullwidth commercial at in place of at sign
rationale: Unicode variant: U+FF20 looks like an at sign but is not the ASCII character; without the ASCII separator the grammar is not met.

reasons: RFC 5322 grammar is ASCII; internationalized mailbox rules were not read.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: Read RFC 6531 (internationalized email) and decide whether lookalike separators are in scope.

provenance.inference: Non-ASCII characters in addresses are covered by a later specification (RFC 6531) that was not read. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.
